subject: development-studies
intro: Development studies leads into the international aid, policy and research worlds: people paid to measure poverty, design programmes, and argue — with evidence — about what actually lifts countries up.

roles.title: Urban and Regional Planners
roles.what: Develop comprehensive plans and programs for the use of land and physical facilities of jurisdictions such as towns, cities, counties and metropolitan areas.
roles.where: The urbanisation topic in the social development unit and the SDG case studies teach the growth-management questions planners answer, while measuring development with GDP and HDI frames how planners argue for infrastructure investment.

roles.title: Economists
roles.what: Conduct research and formulate plans addressing economic problems related to the production and distribution of goods and services or monetary and fiscal policy, processing economic and statistical data with sampling and econometric methods.
roles.where: The economic development unit — agriculture and industry, aid, trade and investment, debt and dependency — plus the measurement unit's GDP work are the intellectual core, and evaluating development projects trains the analysis economists formalise.

roles.title: Sociologists
roles.what: Study human society and social behaviour by examining the groups, social institutions and organisations people form, tracing how group activities shape and are shaped by their individual members.
roles.where: Gender and development, inequality within and between countries, and governance and corruption from the syllabus are the research fields sociologists publish in, with the SDG evaluation work teaching the evidence discipline behind it.

roles.title: Social and Community Service Managers
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate the activities of social service programs or community outreach organisations, overseeing budgets, policies on participant involvement, program requirements and benefits.
roles.where: The social development unit's education and health outcomes work and the SDG unit's project evaluation are the design and accountability skills these managers use to run community programmes and report to funders.

roles.title: Fundraisers
roles.what: Organise activities to raise funds or gather donations for an organisation, designing promotional materials and raising awareness of the organisation's work, goals and financial needs.
roles.where: The aid and investment topics in the economic development unit and the SDG case studies give fundraisers the credible development narratives and evidence donors demand before they commit money.
